correctness.rationale: Ordinary partial composition gives f^2 empty exactly when domain and image are disjoint. For a k-point domain d_1<...<d_k with complement e_1<...<e_m, m=n-k, encode x_i=d_i-i and j_i by f(d_i)=e_(j_i). Regressiveness and disjointness give j_i<=x_i, and isotonicity gives weak increase of the j_i. Conversely x_i+i restores the domain in {2,...,n}, the same complement restores the images, and both constraints hold. Reversal and subtraction by one give the stated two-row boxed plane partition, including the empty k=0 case and the all-zero box at k=n-1. The rectangular product gives the two binomial expressions. Vandermonde normalizes the distribution: K is hypergeometric, drawing n-1 objects from two classes of size n each, so its mean and variance agree with the stated formulas. A regressive finite chain map is nilpotent exactly when all defined steps are strict, and shifting its domain down by one identifies these maps with all regressive isotone partial maps on n-1 elements. The large Schröder and Catalan sequences have the same power n^(-3/2) in their asymptotics, so the claimed exponential ratio follows.
residual_risks: The finite captured results through n=9 are supplemental. Domain size is not image rank for these partial maps; the moment law is for the domain only.

evidence: A domain of k elements means k vertical steps; a path ending at (n,n) has exactly n-k diagonals. Expanding the diagonals of an HV-free path gives a no-diagonal path with n-k peaks, hence exactly n-k horizontal segments. Theorem 3.8 evaluates that number. evidence: The mapping before Theorem 3.1 puts j in the domain for a vertical step at level j, and in the image for a horizontal step at that level. The inverse construction explicitly distinguishes the case of a horizontal run followed by a vertical step when j is in both.

In the frozen regressive class, every square-zero map already omits 1: if 1 is defined it is fixed. After translating labels by one, the type I encoding therefore covers exactly the desired subclass when restricted to paths with no consecutive H,V steps.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A type I path never goes above the diagonal. At a fixed level all horizontal steps occur in one run; it has a vertical exit exactly when that level is in the domain. So an image/domain intersection is exactly an H,V pair. Every diagonal replacement D -> HV stays in the allowed half-plane and preserves endpoints. If the input has no HV, each peak of the expanded path comes from a replaced diagonal; turning each peak back into a diagonal recovers an HV-free path. This is a reversible local translation, not a comparison of unrelated coefficient values.

originality.rationale: The core square-zero domain census is a direct specialization of the published Laradji–Umar partial-map path bijection together with their evaluated horizontal-segment refinement. The overlap is not inferred merely from identical Narayana numbers: the source explicitly records domain by the levels of vertical steps and image by the levels of horizontal steps. Thus square-zero amounts exactly to avoiding a horizontal step immediately followed by a vertical step. Expanding each diagonal step into horizontal then vertical, with inverse obtained by collapsing every peak, reduces this exact domain-conditioned subclass to the paths counted in Theorem 3.8 with n-k horizontal segments. The remaining moment and rarity claims are direct consequences of the resulting known row and the known Schröder count, not a distinct enumerative remainder.
residual_risks: The separate cited technical-report copy was inaccessible. The negative verdict rests instead on a checked, explicit implication of the accessible preprint, not on the access failure. Historical occurrence of the square-zero terminology itself is not determined.

value.rationale: The square-zero statistic is natural, but the exact spectrum here is mechanically implied by the existing path model and its evaluated Narayana refinement. The alternative two-row proof gives another standard encoding, not an independently useful unknown invariant or a new structural consequence beyond that implication. The moment formulas are textbook hypergeometric moments and the rarity is a direct comparison of the existing Catalan and shifted Schröder enumerations. No substantive distinct remainder is established by this frozen finding.
residual_risks: This does not negate the usefulness of studying higher nilpotency indices or simultaneous domain/image statistics; neither is established as a distinct result here.
